text: Personal Agent Protocol — or Poppy for short — has gained real momentum since we first announced this new standard with our initial design partners Meta, Genesys, Instinct, NiCE, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe, and Walmart last month. Poppy enables personal agents to interact with companies through business agents, websites, and APIs and today we’re excited to announce that: Version 1.0 of Poppy reflects what design partners have learned over the past five weeks as they’ve tested the drafts against real websites, APIs, and agents. The protocol defines how personal agents connect with companies that implement it, providing clear and comprehensive access to everything they offer, largely built with existing standards like MCP, OpenAPI, and UCP. With authentication through OAuth, customers control what personal agents can and can’t do, and can manage their access over time. Since the initial draft, we’ve: With v1.0, any company can implement Poppy on its own and immediately start delivering a better experience for customers who use Muse. Our implementation kit walks you through setup and includes a validator to check your work. Shopify powers businesses in more than 175 countries, and every Shopify store supports Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) by default. As more shopping moves to personal agents, every Shopify store now automatically publishes a Poppy file, so merchants don’t need to do any extra implementation. UCP and Poppy complement each other. UCP handles the shopping itself, like finding products, filling a cart, and checking out. Poppy handles what happens before that, when an agent shows up at a store, says who it is, and finds out what it’s allowed to do. Shopify co-authored Poppy’s commerce extension, which links the two protocols. It lets an agent shop as a guest or sign in with the customer’s account, and it makes the agent ask the customer before taking certain actions, so it only acts with their permission. It also connects to UCP Ask, so a shopper’s agent can talk directly to the store’s agent. A number of businesses are now live with Poppy: We’re so grateful to all the companies that are contributing to this new standard, and excited to welcome more to our design partnership. As personal agents take on more of our everyday tasks, companies need clear, secure ways to work with them while continuing to deliver a trusted experience. Poppy gives them that foundation — so the company and the personal agent can get the job done for the customer they share.
